summary: The pre-market read is 58.77, caution, with the risk-on regime intact and model confidence at 0.9134 — 4.07 above yesterday's 54.70 close and 4.84 over the month. Almost the entire rise is cross-asset: 5 of 8 legs trigger (0.625) after bitcoin fell 1.55282 percent over 24 hours and copper fell 0.6851 percent overnight, lifting that dimension from 0.375 to 0.625 and 3.75 points of the total. Breadth moved the other way, above-MA200 slipping to 0.4452 and the new-low ratio rising to 0.0641, so equity structure climbs from 59.81 to 61.44. The 2026-10-28 US close was broadly higher (SPY up 0.3443 percent, MU up 5.8648 percent, AMD up 3.2449 percent, AVGO up 2.7693 percent, NVDA down 1.1746 percent), and 14 of 22 sectors and themes advanced while 8 fell at a mean of 0.4627 percent. The divergence is China: all 11 A-share names closed lower on 2026-10-29 at a mean of 6.3053 percent, erasing the prior session's 6.3074 percent gain. GDP and Personal Income and Outlays at 12:30Z decide whether the December hike priced at 4.03 against 3.88 becomes conviction rather than a level.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation rises from 0.375 to 0.625 with 5 of 8 legs triggering, contributing 9.38 points and single-handedly explaining 3.75 of today's 4.07. The dollar index at 121.3202, the real rate at 2.64 and small-cap relative weakness at -7.9905 (a 63-session relative-strength reading, not a one-day move) are the three chronically triggering legs; bitcoin and copper turning negative overnight supply the fourth and fifth.

Macro at 74.17 remains the highest weighted risk dimension: the 10-year at 4.99, the 2-year at 4.70, a 10-year minus 2-year spread of 0.29 and the real rate at 2.64. But the rate and credit series stop at 2026-10-27, so no post-FOMC yield move on 10-28 has entered the score — the largest blind spot in the current reading.

Equity structure climbs from 59.81 to 61.44 against the index tape: the above-MA200 share falls to 0.4452, the new-low ratio rises to 0.0641 against 0.0256 yesterday, and new highs stay at 0.0064. The advance is narrowing.

All 11 A-share names closed lower on 2026-10-29, mean 6.3053 percent, median 6.3887 percent, with 688525.SH down 15.7927 percent and 300475.SZ down 8.0431 percent — a full round trip from 2026-10-28, when all 11 rose at a mean of 6.3074 percent. Earnings dispersion is the mechanism: GigaDevice Q3 net profit up 728.93 percent year on year but down 21 percent quarter on quarter, Victory Giant Q3 down 52 percent and Jingsheng down 68.65 percent.

Liquidity and credit hold at 66.37: HY OAS 3.18 from 3.30 and IG OAS 0.88 from 0.90 keep tightening, so credit is not confirming the equity tension, while the Fed balance sheet at 6753604 and reverse repo at 0.176 keep draining liquidity.

supporting_signals.claim: Semis led overnight: MU up 5.8648 percent, AMD up 3.2449 percent and AVGO up 2.7693 percent, consistent with Samsung's guidance of memory tightness into 2028 — the AI hardware chain remains where the money is.

Of 22 sectors and themes 14 advanced and 8 fell at a mean of 0.4627 percent and a median of 0.2707 percent, led by data centers at 3.6818 percent, AI infrastructure at 3.3536 percent and semis at 2.6761 percent — the top three are all compute and data-centre exposure.
Volatility keeps falling: VIX 17.52 from 18.39, realized vol at 9.9722, leaving the volatility dimension at 30.95 — the lowest weighted risk block.
Rates edged lower while credit spreads tightened: the 10-year at 4.99 from 5.00 and HY OAS at 3.18 from 3.30 improved together.

contradicting_signals.claim: Breadth diverges from the index: the advance is carried by a few heavyweights while the above-MA200 share at 0.4452 and the new-low ratio at 0.0641 deteriorate — a structure the risk_on label can make look healthier than it is.

The two flipped legs do not describe a coherent haven bid: gold at -0.1333 does not trigger gold_up and SPY at 0.3443 percent does not trigger spy_down, so a move from 3 to 5 triggers looks more like intraday commodity and crypto noise than a broad repricing.

Regional risk appetite runs the other way: all 11 A-share names fell at a mean of 6.3053 percent against a broadly higher US close, so the Asian selling looks domestic — earnings and profit-taking rather than global liquidity.

The hike pricing is oddly shaped: FedWatch puts the 2026-12-16 meeting at an implied 4.03 with a probability of 1.0 on the 4.13 bucket, yet change_1d is 0.0 across buckets, so this is a level rather than an intraday repricing signal and cannot stand alone as hike confirmation.

what_changed_today: The score moves from 54.70 to 58.77 with a 1-day change of 4.07: cross-asset contributes 3.75, equity structure 0.326, macro slips 0.004, and the other three blocks are unchanged.
Two cross-asset legs flipped overnight: bitcoin moved from 0.70761 to -1.55282 over 24 hours and copper from 0.8985 to -0.6851, taking the trigger count from 3/8 to 5/8.
A-shares reversed wholesale: all 11 rose at a mean of 6.3074 percent on 2026-10-28 and all 11 fell at a mean of 6.3053 percent on 2026-10-29, the two sessions almost exactly symmetric.

Samsung extended its memory-tightness guidance to 2028 and raised AI semiconductor capex on its earnings call, yet the stock fell more than 6 percent intraday and the memory basket's Asia leg closed down 0.7548 percent — the same day MU rose 5.8648 percent in the US.
watch_next: GDP and Personal Income and Outlays at 12:30Z on 2026-10-29 are the day's top-tier variables; a hot inflation component would turn the December hike at 4.03 against 3.88 from a level into live momentum.
AMZN, INTC, COIN, SBUX, RBLX and RIVN report from 12:00Z, shifting the AI capex revenue test from Samsung to the US hyperscalers; the next session brings XOM, CVX and ABBV.
Whether cross-asset holds 5/8: the dollar at 121.3202 and the real rate at 2.64 are the stickiest legs, and a reversal in bitcoin or copper decides whether 0.625 falls back to 0.375.
Whether A-shares see follow-through selling after the 6.3053 percent one-day give-back, watching whether 688525.SH (down 15.7927 percent) and 603986.SH (down 4.7916 percent) find support.
Breadth is the most likely second engine: if the new-low ratio at 0.0641 keeps rising and the above-MA200 share breaks 0.4452, equity structure replaces cross-asset as the top contributor.

bull_case.title: Bull case: cross-asset legs revert and breadth repairs
points: Bitcoin and copper recover the overnight drop, the trigger count returns to 3/8, cross-asset goes from 0.625 back to 0.375 and the score falls below 55.
HY OAS holds 3.18 and VIX stays below 17.52, with credit and volatility still underwriting risk appetite.
A-shares stabilise after the 6.3053 percent give-back and the Asia legs stop dragging the memory and robotics baskets.

base_case.title: Base case: caution range, 55 to 62
points: Cross-asset stays at 0.625 because the dollar at 121.3202 and the real rate at 2.64 will not clear, leaving the score near 58.77.
Breadth erodes slowly with the new-low ratio at 0.0641, but HY OAS at 3.18 does not widen, so the model stays caution rather than high_risk.
A-shares track the external tape without another 6.3053 percent one-day give-back.

bear_case.title: Bear case: hot inflation confirms the December hike
points: GDP and Personal Income and Outlays come in hot, the December hike at 4.03 becomes consensus and the 10-year breaks above 4.99.
The new-low ratio climbs from 0.0641 and the above-MA200 share breaks below 0.4452, pushing equity structure and macro in the same direction.
A-share selling continues with all 11 names down at a mean of 6.3053 percent, the score clears 65 and the regime shifts from risk_on to late_cycle.
